_about: The dashboard To-Do feed. Refreshed at every Rule 9 checkpoint alongside the session handoff — this is the handoff distilled into plain language for the 📋 button on every tab. Split For Sam (curation / decisions only a human makes) and For Fable (engineering, the next session picks up).
_status: SkyView got two rounds of scrutiny on 2026-09-06 and came out of both with real fixes. A computer-use session logged sixteen findings: four were genuine and are fixed — the details panel no longer drops you into the middle of a course you just opened, there is now a way back from a course to its discipline (Escape only ever worked if you had arrived by keyboard), every discipline stopped paying a wasted failed download before its descriptions load, and the M-ID chip explains what it means. Two of its findings were not defects at all, and the one it ranked most serious was wrong in an instructive way: it 'corrected' a figure that was already right for the file it named, having measured a different one. Chasing that down found something nobody had noticed — one of the two data files behind the map is twelve days older than the other, which is why the discipline tables and the map can disagree, and that needs a decision. Sam then drove SkyView himself and reported five more: hovering a college course showed the same card every time, the background turned purple when you picked something, typing one more letter of 'welding' made the main intro course vanish from the search, the side panel reopened itself after you hid it, and the results list stopped at 60. All five are fixed, and the panel now also lists similar courses in level order, beginning before advanced.

items.text: You ruled 'All three' on where agency skill statements come from — published agency standards, ACE exhibits, and entered by the MAP team — and flagged it for follow-up. The open question is what wins when the three disagree about the same certification. That answer shapes the course outline's comparison panel, so the next session will need it early.

Three welding merge candidates are queued for a faculty reviewer, not for a session: Introduction to Welding (24 colleges) absorbing Introduction to the Welding Processes (2) and Intro-Welding Processes (1), and the Intermediate Shielded Metal Arc Welding pair behind it. A fourth pair shares a title but is flagged as NOT mergeable — one is credit and one is noncredit, which makes them different courses. kb/merge_candidates/2026-09-05/report.md.

The re-mint approval view is designed and routed through Governance, not built. You approve candidates and the cron applies them; there is no fire button, because a re-mint cannot be undone the way an ordinary correction can. Worth a read before it is built — it names what each candidate must show you, including what the plan was checked against, which is exactly the thing that was missing this week.

Build the course outline on double-click: a layered panel with the MAP-Generated label on every synthetic field, proficiency levels on the course and on each skill, thin skills kept with a confidence chip, and a certification-first way in beside the course-first one. Double-click currently opens the discipline work surface, so split it — a course opens the outline, empty ground keeps today's behavior.

Build the re-mint approval queue against the four-item checklist in its decision record: a register row owning the approval, the surface mapped the moment the first write lands, an insert-only rollback, and a test asserting the view writes approvals and nothing else.
docs/roadmap_archive.md is 575 KB against a 150 KB budget — the largest thing the docs lint flags, and pure history. It is a safe compaction whenever a session has spare room.

Two data files sit behind SkyView and one is twelve days older than the other, so the discipline tables and the map can report different counts for the same discipline — 43 apart on Health. Nothing rebuilds the older one on a schedule. This is your standing question about whether the daily run should rebuild the map's layout, now with a visible cost. Until you decide, we rebuild both together or neither.

Five smaller SkyView items are design calls rather than bugs, so they are yours: the search chips look like a trail you can click back through but only their × does anything; only a course's title is clickable in a list row, not the whole row; a course you have picked up has nowhere to drop it inside the panel, only on the map; Recenter re-centres on the chip rather than on what the panel is showing; and pressing Enter in the search closes the suggestions instead of keeping them open.

The panel's new Similar courses list reads levels out of course titles, which is the only place we hold them — 44% of welding titles say beginning, intermediate or advanced and the rest say nothing. When the course outline lands, feed its level field back into this list so the ladder stops depending on the wording of a title.
